sections.content: How many people stayed in Burton upon Trent after gaining qualifications?

Burton upon Trent is a medium-sized town in the West Midlands. Burton upon Trent does not have its own university.

Burton upon Trent has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Burton upon Trent ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 3,575 state-school pupils from Burton upon Trent who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 995 (28%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,055 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Burton upon Trent to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Burton upon Trent's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Burton upon Trent in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Burton upon Trent move to?

Of Burton upon Trent's graduates, 350 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those graduates (14%) were living fairly locally, in the Burton upon Trent travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Burton upon Trent's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 230 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 95 of those qualified non-graduates (41%) were living fairly locally, in the Burton upon Trent travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Burton upon Trent's GCSE cohort:

  • 280 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands
  • 190 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the East Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 21% of graduates and 19% of qualified non-graduates living in Burton upon Trent had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 805 graduates and 990 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Burton upon Trent. This is compared with the 995 graduates and 1,055 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 78% of the graduates had also lived in Burton upon Trent as GCSE pupils, while 21% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Burton upon Trent in 2018 to 2019, 81% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 19% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
